File SPEC.md · 235 lines · 3,359 wordsWritten 2026-11-07, between the research lanes and Phase A

# SPEC — José Ochoa portfolio site (v1, written 2026-11-07 by the orchestrator)

Read BRIEF.md first. This file is the contract every build lane follows. If the spec and your judgment
disagree on something small, follow the spec; on something big, do the spec's version and leave a note in
`lanes/notes/<your-lane>.md`.

## 0. The thesis (why this site exists)

Epoch AI is forming its first in-house design team (Head of Design posting open since June 2026, two
designers announced, a Website PM posting since September). Their stated pain: "Our researchers and
developers use Claude to change the site directly, and part of this job is keeping that fast without the
site becoming incoherent." Their products: 17+ data explorers built on an in-house D3 chart library, a
claim-first stat-card grammar with confidence intervals, light-only, charts that crop on phones.

José's two strongest pieces answer that pain directly:
1. **CFC Bakery Orders** — a production ordering system he designed and shipped by directing Claude
   agents, with reviewer gates, a 6,089-assertion harness and a 2,121-row assumptions register.
   One designer, zero developers, live store on 2026-11-01.
2. **The CFC design system** — "one system in both directions": theme.json → CSS variables → Figma
   variables, held in parity by a drift checker and an AI hook so nobody (human or agent) can hardcode a value.

So the portfolio's positioning line is: **"I design systems that stay coherent at AI speed."**
Tagline alternatives the copy lane may refine: "Designer. Ships production." / "Design, specified
to the point where agents can build it and reviewers can prove it."

The site must SHOW this. Every number is computed from real data (git logs, GitHub issues, the Figma
file, Epoch's own CSV). Every figure has provenance (source, date, download). The site itself behaves
like a small Epoch-style data product about José's work. AI-in-the-workflow is shown through process
artefacts (prompts, hand-offs, review scores, co-author trailers), never claimed in adjectives.

## 1. Audience and tone

Reader: Epoch's Head of Design (or hiring panel) skimming on a laptop, maybe a phone, 3–6 minutes.
Voice: first person, plain English, specific, calm. Claim-first headlines in sentence case
("142 days from first commit to a live store"). Numbers over adjectives. Never "passionate",
"cutting-edge", "leverage", "seamless". Short paragraphs (≤3 sentences). Honest about trade-offs
(the retro's "change/drop" lists are a feature, not a weakness). Spell "José". Use "the deli lead"
rather than staff names. No customer data, no household finance figures, no partner photo.

## 2. Information architecture (static multi-page site, served from repo root on GitHub Pages)

```
/                         Home — hero chart + stat cards + selected work + how I work + contact
/work/bakery-orders/      Case study 1 (flagship) — scrollytelling, 8 charts, screenshots, Figma
/work/design-system/      Case study 2 — one system in both directions (tokens, parity, hook)
/work/epoch-explorer/     Study for Epoch — "Notable AI models, redrawn for a phone" (interactive)
/process/                 How I work with AI — the method, evidence, lessons, and this site's own build log
/about/                   Bio, timeline, location/overlap, languages, contact
/404.html
```
Each folder has an `index.html` so URLs have no extension. Secondary projects (Project Net, the nanny
funnel) appear as compact cards on Home ("More work") — no dedicated pages in v1.

## 3. Visual system (own identity; compatible with scientific/editorial sites, not a copy of Epoch)

Fonts (Google Fonts, one `<link>`): **Instrument Serif** (display, 400 + italic), **Geist**
(text/UI 400/500/600), **Geist Mono** (numbers, axis labels, eyebrows, code; 400/500).
URL: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist:wght@400;500;600&family=Geist+Mono:wght@400;500&family=Instrument+Serif:ital@0;1&display=swap

Color tokens (define in `assets/css/tokens.css` on `:root`; dark under BOTH
`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) {…} }` AND `:root[data-theme="dark"] {…}`):

| token | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| --paper | #F6F5F1 | #121412 |
| --paper-2 (cards/alt sections) | #EDEBE4 | #1B1E1B |
| --paper-3 (hover/inset) | #E4E1D8 | #242824 |
| --ink | #121412 | #F1EFE9 |
| --ink-2 | #4A4F4B | #BDBAB1 |
| --ink-3 (muted/meta) | #7A807B | #8A8C86 |
| --line | #DAD6CC | #2C302C |
| --accent | #2A78D6 | #3987E5 |
| --accent-ink (text on paper) | #1C5CAB | #6DA7EC |
| --accent-soft | #DCE9F8 | #17304F |
| --series-1..8 | #2a78d6 #eb6834 #1baf7a #eda100 #e87ba4 #008300 #6250d6 #e34948 | #3987e5 #d95926 #199e70 #c98500 #d55181 #008300 #9085e9 #e66767 |
| --seq-100..700 (blue ramp) | #cde2fb #b7d3f6 #9ec5f4 #86b6ef #6da7ec #5598e7 #3987e5 #2a78d6 #256abf #1c5cab #184f95 #104281 #0d366b | same steps; pick the lighter end for dark |
| --good / --warn / --bad | #1a7f37 / #b7791f / #c62828 | #3fb950 / #d4a72c / #ff6b6b |

These series colors come from the validated dataviz palette (`/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.319/039104e58e73864ab5cfa2728a71e274/dataviz/references/palette.md`). Charts use series slots in fixed order; a single-series chart uses --accent.

Type scale (fluid): `--fs-display: clamp(2.75rem, 1.5rem + 5.5vw, 6rem)` (Instrument Serif, line-height .98, letter-spacing -.015em) · `--fs-h1: clamp(2.25rem, 1.4rem + 3vw, 3.75rem)` · `--fs-h2: clamp(1.625rem, 1.2rem + 1.6vw, 2.375rem)` · `--fs-h3: 1.25rem` · `--fs-body: 1.0625rem` line-height 1.6 · `--fs-small: .9rem` · `--fs-meta: .78rem` (mono, uppercase, letter-spacing .08em). Headings h1/h2 in Instrument Serif, h3+ in Geist 600. Numbers in stat cards: Instrument Serif at 3–4.5rem with tabular figures via Geist Mono for units.

Spacing: 4px base; `--space-1..10` = 4 8 12 16 24 32 48 64 96 128. Section padding `clamp(4rem, 8vw, 8rem)`.
Layout: `--w-content: 1120px`, `--w-prose: 680px`, side gutter `clamp(16px, 4vw, 40px)`. Charts may bleed to content width inside prose sections (`.bleed`).
Radius: 6px controls, 12px cards, 999px pills. Borders 1px `--line`; no drop shadows except tooltips.
Motion: reveal-on-scroll (opacity+8px translate, 500ms ease-out, stagger 60ms), chart draw-in on first intersection, count-up on stat numbers (900ms), View Transitions API for same-origin navigation (`@view-transition { navigation: auto; }`), all disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Theme toggle in the header (sun/moon icon button), persisted to localStorage, applied before first paint (inline script in `<head>`), dispatches `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('themechange'))` so charts re-render.
Dark mode is a first-class, selected design, not a filter.

Absolute paths starting with `/` (the site is served from the domain root `https://joseocfc.github.io/`).
Header collapses to a hamburger under 768px. Skip link, focus-visible rings (2px --accent), landmarks, alt text on all images, `aria-label` on icon buttons. Lighthouse a11y target ≥ 95.

## 5. Components (CSS classes in `assets/css/components.css`; markup conventions)

- `.eyebrow` — mono meta line above headings ("Case study · 2026").
- `.hero` — display headline + 1-paragraph dek + hero figure.
- `.stat-card` — `<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">…</p><p class="stat-value" data-count="1503">1,503</p><p class="stat-claim">…</p><footer class="stat-meta">source · date</footer></article>`; grid `.stat-grid` (auto-fit minmax 220px).
- `.figure` — the chart frame (see §6).
- `.toc` — sticky in-page table of contents on ≥1024px (left rail), horizontal scroll chips on mobile; highlights current section via IntersectionObserver.
- `.media` — screenshot frame: `<figure class="media"><img …><figcaption>…</figcaption></figure>`; `.media--phone` (max 390px wide centered), `.media--browser` (thin top bar with three dots), `.media-row` (2–3 across, wraps).
- `.quote` — pull quote with `<cite>` showing the path/source in mono.
- `.callout` — bordered note (`--callout-good/--warn`).
- `.timeline` — vertical list of dated events.
- `.steps` — numbered process ladder.
- `.tag` — pill.
- `.card` / `.work-card` — image + eyebrow + title + one-line + tags; whole card is a link.
- `.diagram` — inline SVG system diagrams (use currentColor and the tokens; no raster).
- `.case-nav` — prev/next at case-study end.
- Buttons: `.btn`, `.btn--primary` (accent fill, ink-on-accent white), `.btn--ghost`.

## 6. Figure anatomy and chart API (lane "charts" owns `assets/js/charts/`, `assets/css/charts.css`)

Markup every page uses:
```html
<figure class="figure" data-chart="timeline" data-src="/data/bakery-metrics.json" id="fig-timeline">
  <header><p class="eyebrow">Figure 1 · Commits per day</p>
    <h3 class="figure-title">142 days from first commit to a live store</h3>
    <p class="figure-sub">Daily commits across all branches, with milestones. October alone holds 1,174 of 1,503.</p></header>
  <div class="chart" role="img" aria-label="…one-sentence description…"></div>
  <figcaption>…one-sentence takeaway…</figcaption>
  <footer class="figure-foot"><span>Source: git log --all, computed 2026-11-07</span>
    <span class="figure-actions"><button data-action="table">Table</button><a data-action="download" download>Data</a></span></footer>
</figure>
```
`assets/js/charts/index.js` finds every `[data-chart]`, fetches `data-src` (cached per URL), and calls the registered renderer `render(chartEl, data, ctx)` where `ctx = { theme, reduced, width, tooltip, fmt, colors }`. Core responsibilities: ResizeObserver re-render (debounced), re-render on `themechange`, draw-in only on first intersection, a shared HTML tooltip (`.chart-tip`), the Table toggle (renders an accessible `<table>` from the renderer's `table()` output below the chart), and Data download (Blob of the JSON slice the renderer used). All colors read from CSS variables via `getComputedStyle` at render time, never hardcoded. Thin marks, 2px lines, 4px bar radius at data end, 2px gap between stacked segments, recessive grid, direct labels where ≤4 series, legend always for ≥2 series, one axis (never dual-axis), log scale labelled in powers where used. Numbers formatted with thin thousands separators. Axis/legend text in `--ink-3` mono `.72rem`. Follow the dataviz skill references at `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.319/039104e58e73864ab5cfa2728a71e274/dataviz/references/` (marks-and-anatomy.md, interaction.md, anti-patterns.md).

Renderers (name → data → form):
1. `timeline` — bakery `commits_by_day` + `milestones` → daily bars (accent), milestone markers with labels (top 6 at desktop, 3 at mobile, rest in tooltip), brush-free, x = date, y = commits (linear; note the 307 spike with a broken-axis label is NOT allowed — instead let the spike stand and annotate it).
2. `growth` — `assertion_count_over_time` and `assumptions_register_rows_over_time` → two small multiples (not dual axis), step/area lines, end labels "6,089 assertions" / "A2121".
3. `issues` — `issues[]` → cumulative opened vs closed lines (series-1 opened, series-2 closed), with the gap shaded, plus median-days-to-close as a note.
4. `heat` — `commits_by_hour` × weekday matrix derived from... (the JSON has by_hour and by_weekday separately; render two small bar charts side by side: by hour (24 bars) and by weekday (7 bars), sequential accent; caption "nights and Mondays").
5. `rounds` — `review_gate.mentions_in_records` → horizontal bars: 1 round 90 · 2 rounds 69 · 3 rounds 18 · 4 rounds 2 · 5 rounds 9 · 10/10 4.
6. `types` — `commits_by_type` → single stacked horizontal bar (100%) with direct labels; docs 734 called out honestly.
7. `models` — `ai_coauthorship.by_model` → horizontal bars sorted desc, note "1,482 of 1,503 commits carry a Claude co-author trailer".
8. `loc` — `loc_by_area` → horizontal bars: tests 62,396 vs includes 50,116 vs docs 51,114 …
9. `ds-commits` — design-system-metrics.json commits_by_day with a vertical marker at 2026-07-17 "v1.0 frozen" and the DS window shaded (2026-06-25 → 2026-08-21).
10. `tokens` — design-system token families → horizontal bars (counts by family) or a dot matrix.
11. `build-log` — this site's own build: lanes as a Gantt (start/end per lane from `data/build-log.json`).
The Epoch explorer is a separate module (`assets/js/epoch-explorer.js`) with its own spec in §8.

1. What I looked at (facts observed 2026-11-07, neutral tone, no snark): at 390px the chart crops at ~2010; label collisions at the frontier; settings become a 'Customize graph' button but the plot does not reflow; copy says 3,200+ in one place and 3,700+ in another; Trends header date vs card data dates.
2. The rebuilt chart (interactive, D3): scatter of training compute (log y, FLOP) vs publication date from `data/epoch/notable_models.json` (trimmed from `research/epoch-data/notable_ai_models.csv` — keep: name, date, domain, organization, country, compute, parameters, dataset size, notability, confidence; drop rows without compute+date). Controls (one row above, wrap on mobile → bottom sheet under 768px): colour by (Domain / Organization top-8+Other / Country top-8+Other), range chips (All time / Deep learning era 2010+ / 2020+), label density (Top 12 / Top 30 / Frontier only), regression toggle (OLS on log10 compute vs year for 2010+, with the rate stated in words "×/year" and a 90% CI from the fit). Mobile: the chart reflows (height adapts, x ticks thin, labels drop to Top 6, tap = tooltip), never crops.
   Label rule: candidates ranked by compute within rolling 6-month windows; place with simple collision avoidance (greedy, skip if overlaps); leader lines only when displaced > 8px.
